champigny-december-1870

French troops attack in the snow at Champigny in December 1870, trying to break out of besieged Paris. Édouard Detaille painted this battle in 1879, as part of a wave of paintings in France remembering the war of 1870.
the-charge-of-the-9th-cuirassiers-at-morsbronn

French armored cavalry charge through the narrow streets of the village of Morsbronn on August 6, 1870, in a brave but hopeless attack against Prussian infantry. Édouard Detaille painted this charge in 1873.
the-cemetery-of-saint-privat

French soldiers defend a village cemetery at Saint-Privat against German attackers during the Franco-Prussian War in August 1870. Alphonse de Neuville painted it in 1881 in a lifelike style meant to show how fiercely they fought.
bourbaki-s-army-crossing-into-switzerland

The worn-out French army of General Bourbaki, starved and half frozen, crosses into Switzerland in February 1871 to escape the Germans, and Swiss people took the soldiers in. Édouard Castres, a Swiss painter who was there as a Red Cross volunteer, painted it in 1881.
at-headquarters-outside-paris
German officers rest in a smart French parlor during the siege of Paris, one with his boots on the table beside a piano. Anton von Werner, a German painter who was at the siege, painted it in 1894.
general-faidherbe-at-bapaume
French General Louis Faidherbe rides on a white horse at the Battle of Bapaume in January 1871, one of the few French successes in the late war. Charles Édouard Armand-Dumaresq painted it in 1883.
the-burning-of-the-hotel-de-ville-24-may-1871
The great Paris city hall, the Hôtel de Ville, burns on May 24, 1871, during the last week of the Paris Commune, the radical government of Paris. Léon Sabatier painted the fires in 1873.
the-arrest-of-louise-michel
Louise Michel, a teacher who fought for the Paris Commune, is arrested by soldiers in 1871 and later sent to a prison colony in the Pacific. Jules Girardet painted her capture in 1871.
hope-pierre-puvis-d
A young woman in white sits among ruins, holding a green branch, as a symbol of hope after France's defeat in the war of 1870 and 1871. Pierre Puvis de Chavannes painted it in 1872.
execution-of-communards-at-the-lobau-barracks
Soldiers shoot captured members of the Paris Commune at the Lobau Barracks in May 1871, during the 'Bloody Week' that ended the Commune. Frédéric Théodore Lix drew it in 1871 for a French newspaper.
official-program-woman-suffrage-procession-march-3-1913

A colorful program for the great Woman Suffrage Procession held in Washington on March 3, 1913, the day before Woodrow Wilson became president. About 5,000 women marched down Pennsylvania Avenue demanding the vote.
the-awakening

A woman in a golden gown, a symbol of Liberty, strides across a map of the United States in which the states where women could vote glow in gold. Henry Mayer's cartoon, published in 1915 in Puck magazine, shows the suffrage movement spreading from the West.
lucretia-mott

Lucretia Mott, a Quaker minister and abolitionist, was one of the organizers of the Seneca Falls Convention in 1848, which launched the American women's rights movement. Joseph Kyle painted her portrait in 1842.
president-wilson-says-votes-for-women

A cartoon by Nina Allender, the cartoonist of Alice Paul's National Woman's Party, shows suffragists behind bars after being arrested for picketing outside the White House in 1917. They had held signs asking President Wilson 'How long must women wait for liberty?'
vote-league-of-women-voters
A woman and a child stand in front of the Capitol on a poster for the League of Women Voters. The League was founded in 1920, the year the 19th Amendment gave American women the right to vote.
votes-for-women-a-success

A map of North America, with the states and provinces where women could vote marked, on a suffrage poster from 1917. By then women could vote in many western states, and the poster urges the rest to follow.
life-magazine-cover-february-20-1913

A Life magazine cover from the suffrage-themed issue of February 1913, in black and gold, by Rea Irvin, who later designed the New Yorker's first cover. Magazines like Life helped bring the vote debate to every living room.
vote-for-the-woman-suffrage-amendment

A map shows in yellow the states where women already had equal suffrage in 1915, and the poster urges voters to approve the woman suffrage amendment in November. New York's vote failed that year but passed two years later.
i-didn-t-raise-my-girl-to-be-a-voter
An anti-suffrage poster from 1915, made by opponents of women voting, borrows the title of a famous song. It shows what the suffragists were up against.
we-are-making-a-new-world

A broken, twisted forest of shattered tree stumps stands in a landscape ripped by shell craters, under a bitter-sounding title. Paul Nash painted this in 1918 as an official war artist, and its irony made it one of the best-known pictures of World War I.
the-menin-road

Paul Nash paints a wrecked, muddy landscape near Ypres in Belgium, with flooded craters and splintered trees. Made for the British government's war memorial project, it shows the destruction of the battlefield in 1919.
gas-attack-lievin
A.Y. Jackson, a founding member of Canada's Group of Seven, painted the green haze of a gas attack over the town of Liévin in 1918, while he was a Canadian war artist.
the-pimple-evening

A bare, shell-torn hill called the Pimple glows red in the evening light near Vimy Ridge, where Canadian troops had fought in 1917. A.Y. Jackson, who later helped found the Group of Seven, painted it in 1918.
canadian-gunners-in-the-mud

Canadian gunners push and pull an artillery piece through deep mud at Passchendaele in late 1917, one of the worst battles of the war. Alfred Bastien, a Belgian painter working for the Canadian War Memorials, painted this.
a-cemetery-on-vimy-ridge
A print of a cemetery on Vimy Ridge, the French hill where Canadian soldiers won a famous victory in April 1917. It was made as a record of the war as soon as it ended.
war-in-the-air
A single aeroplane sails among huge clouds in a dreamy, modern view of the war in the sky. C. R. W. Nevinson painted it in 1918 for Canada's war memorial collection.
the-munitions-girls
Women work in a roaring factory filling shells for the war effort in 1918. Stanhope Forbes painted this scene of the many women who took on jobs once done by men while the soldiers were away.
canteen-at-the-front

Soldiers gather in a candlelit American Red Cross canteen at the front in France. Henry Ossawa Tanner, a Black American painter who lived in France, volunteered with the Red Cross and painted this in 1918.
a-battery-shelled

Wyndham Lewis shows an artillery position under fire in sharp, blocky shapes, like a machine of broken glass. He had served as a gunner himself before becoming an official war artist, and he painted this in 1919.
menin-gate-at-midnight

Ghostly soldiers rise out of the fields near the Menin Gate, the great memorial at Ypres to the missing of World War I. Will Longstaff painted this in 1927 and it became one of Australia's most famous war paintings.
a-grave-and-a-mine-crater-at-la-boisselle-august-1917
A huge crater from a mine explosion and a lonely grave mark the old battlefield at La Boisselle, on the Somme. William Orpen, a British official war artist, painted it in 1917.
amiens-the-key-of-the-west
The Australian war artist Arthur Streeton paints the soft green countryside around Amiens, the city that the Allies defended and then used for their big attack of August 1918.
the-bolshevik

A huge worker holding a red flag strides over the crowded rooftops of a Russian city in this symbol of the Bolshevik revolution. Boris Kustodiev painted it in 1920, three years after the Bolsheviks took power.
the-manifesto-of-17-october-1905

Crowds joyfully wave flags and red banners in the streets after Tsar Nicholas II promised civil rights and a parliament in October 1905. Ilya Repin painted this big crowd scene, which captures the hope, and the tension, of Russia's first revolution.
demonstration-on-october-17-1905-study
Ilya Repin's lively early study for his painting of the crowds celebrating Tsar Nicholas II's October Manifesto of 1905, with swirls of red flags.
the-pogrom-of-the-winter-palace

Soldiers and workers rush into the Winter Palace, the home of the Russian government, on the night of October 25, 1917, when the Bolsheviks seized power. Ivan Vladimirov painted it in 1917 as an eyewitness.
lenin-s-funeral
Vladimir Lenin, the leader of the Bolshevik Revolution, lies in his coffin surrounded by red flags and officials in January 1924. Isaak Brodsky painted this memorial scene in 1925.
beat-the-whites-with-the-red-wedge

A red triangle slices into a white circle in El Lissitzky's famous poster, a symbol of the Red Army defeating the White Army in the Russian Civil War. It was made in 1919 and 1920 and mixes politics with modern abstract art.
soviet-propaganda-poster-1920
A Soviet poster of 1920 uses bold colors and cartoon figures in the style of the revolution's propaganda posters, which taught people about the new government in a country where many could not read.
before-october-1917-after-october

A poster compares life before October 1917 and after it, using simple pictures so that everyone could understand the Bolshevik message. It was made by Stepan Mukharsky in 1920, during the Russian Civil War.
bloody-sunday-1905

On January 22, 1905, soldiers fired on peaceful workers marching to the Winter Palace to ask the tsar for help, killing and wounding many, an event that started the Revolution of 1905. Wojciech Kossak painted this scene of Bloody Sunday.
migrant-mother

Florence Owens Thompson sits in a pea-pickers' camp in California in 1936, with her children turned away. Dorothea Lange's photograph for the government became the best-known image of the Great Depression.
farmer-and-sons-walking-in-the-face-of-a-dust-storm-cim

A farmer and his sons walk bent against a huge dust cloud in Oklahoma in April 1936, during the Dust Bowl. Arthur Rothstein took this photograph for the government, which hired photographers to show how hard the Depression was.
toward-los-angeles-california

A man and woman carry their bags along an empty road in California in 1937, with a billboard above them that says 'Next time try the train.' Dorothea Lange's photo shows the ordeal of families who moved west to look for work.
